title: Power Apps: calendar and card layouts for views in model-driven apps
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly reports licensing as unpublished. Microsoft documents that model-driven apps require Power Apps premium use rights; only requirements specific to the new layouts remain undocumented. The roadmap facts and the general environment path and CLI command are supported.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because neither the roadmap nor Microsoft Learn states a licence for the new layouts.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Replace the licensing notes and the opening "Not yet published" in Cost and licensing with: "Model-driven apps require a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights. Microsoft lists Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter as general entitlement options; qualifying Dynamics 365 rights depend on context. Requirements specific to the new layouts are not yet published." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-licensing-faq. In the cost rationale, replace "licensing for the new layouts is not yet published" with "requirements specific to the new layouts are not yet published". Keep cost low: the briefing rates the change, not the existing app entitlement.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to the new layouts.

claims.claim: The roadmap entry describes no additional licence or consumption charge.
claims.quote: Makers can now choose to display their data as a calendar or a stack of cards instead of the default grid layout. Makers can configure these layouts directly in the model driven app designer, giving users more intuitive ways to visualize and work with their data.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page documenting these new layouts was found at review time.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "new view layout"; "model-driven" "calendar" "card" "layouts". Read create-edit-views and results for add-calendar-control and create-card-forms: existing controls, not this planned combined layout feature.

claims.claim: Existing table security applies to the model-driven app data shown by the layouts.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use role-based security for sharing. The fundamental concept in role-based security is that a security role contains privileges that define a set of actions that can be performed on tables within the app.
